title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-amelia-cho
content:
Account: FinTrue (headquartered SF)
Priority segment: mid-market fintechs with 50-500 engineers, latency-sensitive customer-facing AI (support triage, quoting assistant)
Why Redwood?
- They care about predictable latency and cost — public benchmarks (we show 60-80% lower per-token cost on caching + batching for similar models)
- Security needs: SOC2 + optional Private deployment/VPC (talking to security team)
- Use-case fit: quoting assistant + customer-facing chat where 200ms token latency matters
Key contacts (to source):
- Head of ML / Director of Engineering (likely decision maker for infra)
- Product lead for support automation (influence)
- Procurement / Security (final approvers)
Notes from quick research:
- FinTrue raised Series B mid-2023, expansion hiring 2024 (customer success and platform)
- Public blog post: switched to embeddings for 1:many search in 2023 — likely heavy embeddings usage
- Careers page shows ML infra hiring -> good timing for infra conversation
Pain points to target in outreach:
- Ballooning inference costs on current hosted provider (they mentioned 3rd-party API overage in job posting)
- Inconsistent latency across regions -> affects SLAs for clients
- Hard to roll out model updates safely (want canary + A/B)
Outbound email draft v1 (short, cold):
Subject: Cut inference cost + stabilize latency for FinTrue's quoting assistant
Hi <FirstName>,
Quick note — I work on partnerships at Redwood Inference. We help fintech platforms reduce per-token inference costs and guarantee predictable latency for customer-facing flows (think quoting assistants/support chat). I looked at FinTrue's work on embeddings and platform infra growth — seems like the perfect time to look at putting inference on a more predictable stack.
2 quick questions: are you owning inference infra or centrally managed? And would you be open to a 20-25 min sync next week to share a quick cost/latency analysis?
Best,
Amelia

Alternate longer email (with social proof):
Subject: How [peer-firm] cut inference cost 45% while improving 95th pct latency
Hi <FirstName>,
We recently helped [peer-firm in fintech] move from a multi-vendor hosted setup to a Redwood Dedicated pool and achieved ~45% token cost reduction (prefix caching + batching) and improved 95th percentile latency from 420ms to 180ms.
If you own the quoting/support model at FinTrue, I can put together a 15-min, zero-commitment cost/latency sketch for your traffic profile.
Would Wed/Thu next week work?

Call guide / discovery checklist (30 min):
- Introductions + context: what product flows use LLMs? (chat, quoting, summarization)
- Traffic profile: tokens / reqs per minute, peak hours, regional split
- Current infra: hosted API vs self-hosted vs hybrid, any dedicated pools?
- SLOs: p50/p95 latency targets, error budgets, throughput requirements
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS/HSM needs, VPC/air-gapped requirements
- Model lifecycle: how do they handle model upgrades, canaries, rollbacks?
- Cost pain: invoicing surprises, unit cost targets, business impact of cost reduction
Quick objection playbook (notes to self):
- "We're happy with current provider" -> Acknowledge + ask about worst-case scenarios (downtime, cost spikes). Offer a low-effort pilot (shadow traffic or small dedicated pool) and a case study.
- "Security/compliance concerns" -> Emphasize Private deployment & KMS integrations + audit logs; propose a short architecture review with security teams. Offer NDA if needed.
- "Migration cost/effort" -> Offer phased migration: routing small % traffic, automatic fallbacks, and migration runbook. Highlight Redwood Optimize recommendations to minimize perf/regression risk.
- "Pricing" -> Explain pricing levers (batching, caching, quantization) that reduce unit cost without losing quality. Offer a modeled TCO vs current provider for their profile.
Questions to surface during call to qualify for Dedicated/Private: 
- Monthly committed spend target (are they ready for reserved capacity?)
- Need for region isolation (EU-only customers?)
- Data residency or air-gap requirements
- Team readiness: do they have infra engineers to run hybrid/private?
Follow-up cadence (if no response):
- Day 3: brief polite nudge with one-liner and social proof
- Day 7: add value — snippet of a quick perf/cost idea specific to FinTrue (e.g., prefix caching for support flows)
- Day 14: final note, ask for referral if not the right person
To-dos / next steps:
- Build quick cost sketch template for fintech quoting workload (tokens/req distribution typical: ~60 tokens request, 120 tokens response on average) [TODO: ask Priya for template]
- Get peer-firm case study (ask Marcus for intro to Legal for permission)
- Find contact list on LinkedIn + check for overlaps with Redwood account execs
- Draft security one-pager for Private deployment (short checklist for early conversations)
Random scratch ideas:
- Offer a one-off "health check" where we run an anonymized latency/cost benchmark on a sample conversation set they share (no data ingestion)
- Partner webinar targeting fintech infra: "Make inference predictable: cost, latency, and rollouts" — invite FinTrue platform leads
Notes to self (messy):
- Keep emails short — they respond to concrete % savings + time-saved claims
- Use customer names, not generic "industry peers" if possible
- Push for intro to procurement early if they have clear cost-savings story
- If they care about model quality/regression, lead with Redwood's evals + rollback features
References/links to pull in:
- Confluence: /pages/RED-PerfBench-fintech (ask Priya to share)
- Jira: ENG-987 (migration runbook draft)
- Slack thread: #sales-fintech (pin best outreach lines)
